q: In the given figure, ABCD is a rectangle and P is a point on DC such that BC = 24 cm, DP = 10 cm and CD = 15 cm. If AP produced intersects BC produced at Q, then the length of AQ.
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let the length of }}CQ = x\,\& \,\angle PQC = \theta \\ & {\text{In }}\Delta ABQ, \\ & \tan \theta = \frac{{15}}{{24 + x}}.\,.\,.\,.\,.\,\left( {\text{i}} \right) \\ & {\text{Again in }}\Delta PCQ \\ & \tan \theta = \frac{5}{x}\,.\,.\,.\,.\,.\,\left( {{\text{ii}}} \right) \\ & {\text{From equation}}\left( {\text{i}} \right)\,\& \,\left( {{\text{ii}}} \right) \\ & \frac{{15}}{{24 + x}} = \frac{5}{x} \\ & 3x = 24 + x \\ & 2x + 24 \\ & x = 12 \\ & {\text{In }}\Delta ABQ, \\ & {\text{By pythagoras theorem}} \\ & A{Q^2} = A{B^2} + B{Q^2} \\ & = {15^2} + {36^2} \\ & = 225 + 1296 \\ & = 1521 \\ & AQ = 39 \end{aligned}$$

q: In ∆ABC, ∠C = 90°, point P and Q are on the sides AC and BC, respectively, such that AP : PC = BQ : QC = 1 : 2. Then, $$\frac{{{\text{A}}{{\text{Q}}^2} + {\text{B}}{{\text{P}}^2}}}{{{\text{A}}{{\text{B}}^2}}}$$ is equal to:
s: Let the side of BC & CA are 3x and 3y QC = 2x QB = x PC = 2y AP = y In triangle AQC AQ 2 = (3y) 2 + (2x) 2 = 9y 2 + 4x 2 BP 2 = (3x) 2 + (2y) 2 = 9x 2 + 4y 2 AB 2 = (3x) 2 + (3y) 2 = 9x 2 + 9y 2 = 9(x 2 + y 2 ) $${\text{Now, }}\frac{{{\text{A}}{{\text{Q}}^2} + {\text{B}}{{\text{P}}^2}}}{{{\text{A}}{{\text{B}}^2}}} = \frac{{13\left( {{x^2} + {y^2}} \right)}}{{9\left( {{x^2} + {y^2}} \right)}} = \frac{{13}}{9}$$

q: G is the centroid of a triangle ABC, whose sides AB = 35 cm, BC = 12 cm, and AC = 37 cm. The length of BG is (correct to one decimal place):
s: AB = 35 cm, BC = 12 cm and AC = 37 cm 12, 35 and 37 are triplet ABC is a right angle triangle at ∠B = 90° Use appoloneous theorem $$\begin{aligned} & A{B^2} + B{C^2} = 2\left( {A{D^2} + B{D^2}} \right) \\ & {35^2} + {12^2} = 2 \times {\left( {\frac{{AC}}{2}} \right)^2} + 2B{D^2} \\ & {37^2} = 2 \times {\left( {\frac{{37}}{2}} \right)^2} + 2B{D^2} \\ & 2B{D^2} = {37^2}\left( {1 - \frac{1}{2}} \right) \\ & 2B{D^2} = 1369 \times \frac{1}{2} \\ & B{D^2} = \frac{{1369}}{4} \\ & BD = \frac{{37}}{2} \\ & BG = BD \times \frac{2}{3} \\ & BG = \frac{{37}}{2} \times \frac{2}{3} \\ & BG = \frac{{37}}{3} = 12.3{\text{ cm}} \end{aligned}$$
